text: Qt controls for FontLab objects and FontParts-style fonts. Qt loads only at construction. What it holds: the general browsers, previews, features editor and Designspace panel, the Qt lifetime base ( lifecycle ), the pure models, the sequence canvas, and the editors for FontParts-style fonts: font info, groups, kerning, transform, batch and glyph sequence. fontlabapp.fontui.feature_blocks reads and writes exact VFJ feature source through Fontport. Lazy by design: this module imports no editor module and no PythonQt. A factory imports its module only when you call it, which keeps the FontLab 5 s cold-import limit. Fontport: the FontParts editors validate and apply data with fontlab_fontport . That package depends on this one, so it is an optional extra: pip install "fontlab-fontlabapp[fontport]" . Without it, calling one of those factories raises ImportError that names the extra. Everything else here works without Fontport. Moved back (issue 201): fontlab_fontport.ui held these editors for one release. Fontport now has no UI; its ui package only raises ImportError . old: from fontlab_fontport.ui import kerning_editor new: from fontlabapp.fontui import kerning_editor

text: Shared plan and write kernel of the anchor writer scripts. What: the Anchors scripts (Rename Bulk, Center Horizontally, Place From Bounds, Snap To Metrics, Round To Grid, Delete By Name, Mirror Across Masters) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows. Each row can hold one Edit : ("set", name, (x, y)) : move the anchor; add it when it is missing; ("remove", name, None) : delete every anchor with this name; ("rename", name, new) : rename every anchor with this name. collect runs the planner on every editable layer and returns a Plan . require_safe refuses the whole batch before any history exists. apply_work writes all edits as ONE native Undo step and reads every value back. How: apply_work builds every native pin and point first ( prepare ), then calls fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit with operation="geometry" . The commit discloses queued native updates and refuses auto layers in the edit list, glyphs that own an auto layer and bases of auto composites (also through other composites). Then it inits history, runs write , stamps the glyphs, sends one notification and stamps again. unstored is the read-back: a value that FontLab did not keep raises RuntimeError . A failure after history started raises history.PartialWriteError ("... use Edit > Undo"). Why: FontLab cannot Redo an existing anchor moved to 0, 0 (FontLab issue 8527), so require_safe refuses that move. A new pin gets its name-derived appearance now ( anchor_copy.APPEARANCE ), because FontLab infers it only on Redo or reopen. An existing pin keeps its own style and expressions: write edits the existing pin object in place. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time. PythonQt, FontLab and anchor_copy load inside the functions, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. The panel base is in fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model . Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.anchors.panel.model as anchor_panel import fly.ap.anchors.writer as anchor_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): return [anchor_writer.Change("top", "1, 2", "0, 2", ("set", "top", (0, 2)))] class Panel(anchor_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY = "Example", "anchors_example" def planner(self): return planner

text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the anchor writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns AnchorPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Anchors scripts: script controls, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. ERROR_COLOR colours blocked rows; MAX_ROWS limits the preview rows. How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.anchors.writer ( collect , blocked_rows , require_safe ) on every control change, and Apply plans again from live data and writes with anchor_writer.apply_work (one Undo step). Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect in closeEvent . Why: the seven Anchors scripts then hold only their planner, a small panel subclass and main . This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.anchors.panel.ui . So FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast, and tests without Qt can import it. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.anchors.panel.model as anchor_panel class RoundToGrid(anchor_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION = "Round Anchors to Grid", "anchors_round_to_grid", "Round" def build_controls(self): ... def planner(self): ...

What: a subclass sets TITLE , KEY , ACTION (the Apply button text) and HEADERS (3 or 4 columns), and fills in build_controls and planner . Optional hooks: chosen_masters , glyph_names and on_reload . text: Add plain components to EXISTING glyphs, inside the caller's one history step. What: a script that adds components to glyphs that exist (Make Lower Unicase, Set Default Figures) needs a new component shape for each (base glyph, layer). No component constructor is measured on this FontLab build (fl#8505: setGlyphComponents rejects every argument form, addComponent only records a recipe entry; the source has an flShape(glyph, layer) constructor, pyflshape.cpp:66-79 , which is a native probe item and is not used). Two calls: build_components(package, target, wanted, facts) , BEFORE the caller's history.commit . It clones one plain component that the font already has (the prototype), once per NewComponent , and points each detached clone at its base glyph, layer and offset. Nothing is added to the font yet. Refusals raise ValueError and name the target glyph, so a script can show a kept row: an unknown base, a base without that layer, a bad offset, and a font without any plain component ( NO_PROTOTYPE ). add_component(layer, shape) , INSIDE mutate of the caller's history.commit(..., operation="geometry") : it adds one built shape to the target layer and checks that the layer holds one more component of that base. Declare the target layers and glyphs in the commit. The caller's commit is then the ONE Undo step of the edit. NEW glyphs get their components another way: put them in the glyph's own Add Glyph data ( glyph_creation.NewGlyph(components=(Part(...), ...)) ). That works also in a font without any component, and each new glyph is its own Undo step with its components. Why no scratch glyph: a temporary glyph made with fontpr set_glyph adds an Add Glyph Undo step, and flPackage.deleteGlyph removes it outside history, so Redo would put the temporary glyph back ( flcommands.cpp:914,919 ). That path is a native milestone candidate, not shipped behaviour. The cost: an existing glyph in a font without any plain component is refused. Prototype filter: a clone copies the builder state (attached flag, attach anchor, component variation; flcompositeshapesbuilder.cpp:79-93 ) and the shape style (excluded, content lock, non-spacing, boolean operation, opacity; flshape.cpp:1906-1934,2213 ). An attached clone gets its offset overwritten at the next layer update ( fllayer.cpp:1493-1535 ). So a prototype qualifies only when every one of these reads as the default through Python; _qualifies holds the rules: the bound flShape members ( pyflshape.cpp:438-443 ): excluded and contentLocked are the bool False , opacity is 1.0; the fontpr get_glyph VFJ of its glyph ( mcptools_source.cpp:58-79 , a bound Python call; no flShape member reads these fields): the layer's elements match the layer shapes one to one; the element of the prototype has no locked , nonSpacing , booleanOperation , opacity or excluded key with a non-default value, and its component holds only glyphName , layerName and attached: false (no attachAnchor , no off2026Variation ; tags of bin_types.cpp:383,535-545 ; writers flshape.cpp:826-831 , flcompositeshapesbuilder.cpp:1141-1170 ). Anything that cannot be read, or reads otherwise, disqualifies the shape. No qualifying prototype gives the NO_PROTOTYPE kept row. Not measured natively: that a clone of a component is detached (own shapeData , reference count 1), that setting componentGlyph , componentLayer and transform on the detached clone re-targets it, and the Undo/Redo/save/reopen result. build_components has no auto-glyph consent: the edit runs in the caller's commit, whose history.refusal policy refuses auto layers and bases of auto composites. Offline tests prove the call order and the refusals only. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt, fontpr and scripting load when build_components runs. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.creation as component_creation import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) wanted = [component_creation.NewComponent("A", master) for master in package.masters] shapes = component_creation.build_components(package, "a", wanted, facts) target = package.findName("a") layers = [target.findLayer(m) for m in package.masters] def mutate(): for layer, shape in zip(layers, shapes, strict=True): component_creation.add_component(layer, shape) history.commit("Unicase", layers, [target], mutate, operation="geometry", facts=facts)

text: Shared plan, eject and write kernel of the component writer scripts. What: the Components writer scripts (Align By Anchor, Build From Recipes, Copy Offsets Between Masters, Decompose, Nested Finder, Replace Reference, Unlock Lock) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows. A row can hold one edit, which the script's Editor writes: EjectEditor (Decompose, Nested Finder) replaces a component with the parts of its base glyph, one level per press; MoveEditor (Align By Anchor, Copy Offsets) sets the offset of a component that plain_move accepts; other scripts subclass Editor . collect runs the planner on every editable layer and returns a Plan . Auto layers are listed and skipped, never edited. copy_problem gives the reason why the parts of a component cannot be copied safely, or "". It walks every base level as FontLab's builder does: a plain (not auto) base layer, affine transforms only, no composite shape that is not a component, no loop, not deeper than MAX_DEPTH . require_safe refuses the whole batch before any history exists: a glyph that owns an auto layer or is a base of one (also through other composites). apply_work writes all edits through ONE history.commit with operation="geometry" . EjectEditor builds the copies first, gives each removed component with its data and builder as retain= ( history.component_history ), and reads the layers back. How: eject refreshes the component cache, then copies the base parts with ejectTo() BEFORE history opens. keep_raw_state copies back what a native copy drops: the raw node connection bits (FontLab issue 8516), the element note (FontLab issue 8538) and the element name. Inside history, the write only removes the component and inserts the copies at its place. history.commit puts the retained objects first in the notification and asks for deep history, which FontLab's Undo needs for a removed component (FontLab issue 7641). Why: the logic was a private copy in each script. One App module keeps the refusals and the Undo protocol the same in every script that uses it. The generic kernel ( Change , Plan , Editor , apply_work , fmt , plural , layer_of , shown , settle ) lives in fontlabapp.masters.layers.writer ; this module re-exports it, so the Components scripts keep one import. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( history , edit_guards , layer_writer ) at load time. The fontlab module loads inside the functions, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.writer as component_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): rows = [] for shape in component_writer.components(layer): why = component_writer.copy_problem( package, (glyph.name, master), shape, master ) edit = None if why else shape.id name = component_writer.base_of(shape) rows.append(component_writer.Change(name, "", "parts", edit, why)) return rows plan = component_writer.collect(glyphs, masters, planner) facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) component_writer.require_safe(plan.work, facts) component_writer.apply_work( plan.work, "Decompose", facts, component_writer.EjectEditor(unlock=True) )

text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the component writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns ComponentPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Components scripts (Align By Anchor, Build From Recipes, Copy Offsets Between Masters, Decompose, Nested Finder, Replace Reference, Unlock Lock): script controls, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. ERROR_COLOR colours blocked rows; MAX_ROWS limits the preview rows. The helpers are the same objects as in fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model and fontlabapp.metrics.panel.model . How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.components.writer ( collect , blocked_rows , require_safe ) on every control change. Apply plans again from live data, scans the auto-layer facts again and writes with component_writer.apply_work and the script's editor() (one Undo step). Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect in closeEvent . Why: each script then holds only its planner, a small panel subclass and main . This module imports only stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.components.panel.ui . So FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast, and tests without Qt can import it. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.panel.model as component_panel import fly.ap.components.writer as component_writer class Decompose(component_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION, DONE = "Decompose Components", "components_decompose", "Decompose", "Decomposed" HEADERS = ("Glyph · master", "Component", "Becomes") def build_controls(self): ... def planner(self): ... def editor(self): return component_writer.EjectEditor(unlock=True)

text: Pure 2D affine math in Qt's row-vector convention. No Qt import. What it does: Holds a transform as six floats (a, b, c, d, e, f) , the same order as QTransform(m11, m12, m21, m22, dx, dy) . A point maps as x' = a*x + c*y + e and y' = b*x + d*y + f . How to use: concat(first, then) applies first , then then . This is Qt's first * then . apply maps one point. invert gives the inverse. rotation makes a rotation; IDENTITY changes nothing. from_qtransform copies a native QTransform into plain floats. viewport_transform reads a FontLab canvas map as one Affine. Example: apply(concat(glyph_to_canvas, canvas_to_view), x, y) maps one glyph point to widget pixels. Why this design: - Plain tuples keep no native wrapper alive and are safe in paint code. - No Qt import. The module loads in a cold FontLab start (5 s limit) and in tests without PythonQt. Qt classes arrive as arguments. - Every public function rejects non-finite numbers with ValueError by default. A bad native matrix then fails loud, not as a silent bad paint. Pass finite=False only for deliberate raw math. Used by: canvas_rsb , canvas_anchor_rings , drawing . Glyport adopts the same names later ( fontlab_glyport.drawing.context ).

text: Contour copies and Qt path contours of the Contours generator scripts. What: Shadow Copy, Small Caps From Capitals, Superior & Inferior Figures and Tabular Figure Copies copy the contours of a layer through a transform; Outline Effect turns a stroked QPainterPath back into FontLab contours. This module holds those shared parts: contour_shapes gives the own (non-component) shapes that hold contours. copy_contours copies their contours: first the element transform, then the caller's transform. repair_nodes copies the node names and raw node flags back onto each copy. path_contours builds closed flContour objects from the elements of a QPainterPath . How: a contour copy is contour.cloneMapped(...) . FontLab's contour copy can drop node names and raw node flags (fl#8569). repair_nodes copies only these two fields back: the node names and raw node flags. Other node properties, contour names and element names and notes are not copied by copy_contours . restore_shape repairs a whole detached shape, including its shape-data name/note and contour names. It keeps clone selection bits by default; keep_view_state=True restores source selection and active flags. Why: the code was a private copy in five scripts. contour_shapes is not fontlabapp.contours.writer.outline_shapes : that one returns the shapes that an outline script may edit in place, and it keeps shared and scaled shapes out. A copy can use those shapes too, because it maps every contour through its element transform. This module imports only the standard library at load time. path_contours loads fontlab and PythonQt when it runs, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native FontLab behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.copy as contour_copy copies = contour_copy.copy_contours(layer, move) # read before history

text: Measure the vertical extent of a layer from its outline nodes. What: vertical_extent(layer) returns (ymin, ymax) of every contour of every shape of layer , or None when no contour has a node. Why: FontLab keeps flLayer.boundingBox and flShape.boundingBox as a cache. After a Python node move, the cache stays stale, also after notifyChangesApplied (fl#8575, FontLab 9.0.9790). This module never reads a boundingBox and never calls update() , so the read has no side effects. How: each shape's contours are mapped through shape.transform (an affine QTransform, read through m11() … m33() ), so a component counts at its placement, as in masters.layer_contours . Shapes without contours (stickers, empty shapes) give nothing. Nodes come from contour.nodes() as node.x , node.y and their kind: node.isOn() (on-curve), node.isCurve() (cubic control, flNode::Curve ) or else a quadratic control ( flNode::Off , node.isOff() ; flnode.h). The kind decides each segment, not contour.isTT : FontLab sets isTT when any node is a quadratic control, so one contour can mix both kinds (flcontour.cpp). As in FontLab's contour enumerator (flconturenum.h), an implied on-curve midpoint lies only between two consecutive Off nodes. Each segment between two on-curve nodes gives its end y values and its exact y extremes: the roots of the cubic derivative in (0, 1) for two Curve controls, or the one extreme for one Off control. A closed contour also gives its closing segment. Not counted, by design: stroke thickness ( maxThickness , which flShape.boundingBox adds), because zones measure the outline; and the per-contour contour.transform() , which is identity outside an interactive transform (flshapedata.cpp).

text: Shared plan kernel of the outline writer scripts (Contours folder). What: the Contours writer scripts (Round Coordinates, Remove Overlap, Add Extremes, Correct Contour Direction, Straighten Short Curves, Optimize Start Points, Delete Small Contours, Fix Zero Handles, Delete Duplicate Contours, Transform, Slant) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows; the script's Editor writes them through apply_work (one Undo step). This module adds the outline parts to the generic fontlabapp.masters.layers.writer kernel and re-exports that kernel: outline_shapes gives the own contour shapes that a script may edit in place, and a note for every shape that it keeps (shared outline data, scaled or rotated shapes). note_rows turns the notes into rows. node_points and translation read nodes and plain shape moves. collect runs the planner on every chosen layer. A glyph that the geometry policy refuses is listed and skipped as a whole; the other glyphs are still written. With compatible , a glyph whose structure edits would differ between masters is held back ( held_back ). require_safe is a compatibility hook; apply_work discloses queued glyph updates through history (FontLab issue 8537). How: a Change.key names a structure edit (for example the index of a deleted contour). held_back compares the keys of all masters: the masters stay compatible only when every master gets the same keys and every master with a key edit is in scope. Why: the logic was a private copy in each of the eleven scripts. The refusal policy differs from component_writer on purpose: an outline batch skips each refused glyph, with a row that says why, and asks for consent ( allow_bases ) before it edits bases of automatic composites. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( history , edit_guards , layer_writer ) at load time, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. The panel base is in fontlabapp.contours.panel.model . Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.writer as outline_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): shapes, notes = outline_writer.outline_shapes(layer) rows = [outline_writer.Change("nodes", "3", "4", ("nodes", shapes))] return rows + outline_writer.note_rows(notes) plan = outline_writer.collect(glyphs, masters, planner, facts) outline_writer.require_safe() outline_writer.apply_work(plan.work, "Example", facts, ExampleEditor())
title: fontlabapp.contours.writer

text: restore_shape ( source : Any , clone : Any , keep_view_state : bool = False , indexes : Sequence [ int ] | None = None ) -> None Restore fields that FontLab can drop from a detached shape clone. Call after cloning and before adding the clone to a layer. Copy the shape-data note/name, contour names, node names and raw connection flags. By default keep clone node selection bits and shape view state. With keep_view_state=True , copy full source nodeState and shape active and selected flags. Pass indexes to pair a subset of source contours with clone contours, in that order; None pairs all source contours. Example: restore_shape(source, clone, True, indexes=[2, 0]) . Use only a detached clone; mismatched counts raise RuntimeError to avoid storing flags on the wrong nodes.

text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the outline writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns OutlinePanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Contours writer scripts: script controls, the master scope, a "Keep masters compatible" tick for scripts that change the node structure, a consent tick for bases of automatic composites, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. ERROR_COLOR colours blocked rows; MAX_ROWS limits the preview rows. The helpers are the same objects as in fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model . How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.contours.writer.collect on every control change. Apply plans again from live data, scans the auto-layer facts again and writes with outline_writer.apply_work and the script's editor() (one Undo step). A new scan clears the consent tick, because the consent belongs to the glyphs that the user saw. Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect in closeEvent . Why: each script then holds only its own logic, a small panel subclass and main . OutlinePanel is its own class, not a subclass of fontlabapp.components.panel.model 's ComponentPanel : the scope, the ticks, the per-glyph refusal, the error display of Apply and the status texts differ, so a subclass would replace almost every method. This module imports only stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.contours.panel.ui . So FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast, and tests without Qt can import it. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.panel.model as outline_panel import fly.ap.contours.writer as outline_writer class RoundCoordinates(outline_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION, DONE, UNIT = "Round Coordinates", "outlines_round", "Round", "Rounded", "item" def build_controls(self): ... def planner(self): ... def editor(self): ...

text: Shared panel base of the Contours scripts that work on the selected glyphs. What: panel_type() returns SelectionPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of Shadow Copy, Outline Effect, Autohint Selected Layers and Remove PostScript Hints: script controls, a master scope ("Current master" or "All masters"), a consent tick for bases of automatic composites ( BASES_TEXT ), a preview table, a status line and the buttons Use selection, Close and the action. fontlabapp.glyphs.copies.panel_type() returns CopiesPanel , the same base set up for the scripts that create glyph copies. How: the panel binds to the font that is current when it opens and takes the Font window selection. The public facts attribute stores auto-layer facts from construction, reselect() or scan() (explicit Refresh). Use self.facts in plan_rows to avoid a whole-font scan for each control signal. Every control change plans again with the script's plan_rows and fills the table with its cells . The action plans again from the live font and calls the script's write once. Use selection reads the selection again and clears the consent tick, because the consent belongs to the glyphs that the user saw. A refusal ( ValueError , RuntimeError or TimeoutError ) in Use selection or in the action shows its text in the status line. Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect when the panel closes. Why: the four panels differed only in their controls, so each script now holds only its own logic, a small panel subclass and main . The panel is not fontlabapp.contours.panel.model 's OutlinePanel : that one plans outline_writer rows; these scripts plan their own rows. MAX_ROWS is the fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model limit. This module imports only stdlib-only App modules at load time; panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.contours.selection.panel.ui , which imports PythonQt. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.selection.panel.model as selection_panel class ShadowPanel(selection_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION = "Shadow Copy", "generate_shadow", "Add Shadow" def build_controls(self): ... def plan_rows(self, package, masters): ... def cells(self, row): ... def pending(self, todo): ... def write(self, package, rows): ... def result_text(self, result): ...

text: Shared transform writer and preview of Contours > Transform and Slant. What: both scripts apply one affine matrix to the chosen layers. transform_changes plans one layer: one row for its shapes and one row for its anchors. TransformEditor writes the plan; bakes decides per shape how. layer_outline , mapped , outline_path and fit feed the before/after preview. panel_type() returns TransformPanel : the OutlinePanel of fontlabapp.contours.panel.model plus an outline preview of the first glyph that may change. How: every shape gets the composed transform (old shape transform, then the matrix). A shape that bakes accepts then gets shape.applyTransform() : FontLab writes the new nodes and resets the matrix. This is FontLab's own per-shape rule of the layer transform ( fllayer.cpp:6957-6978 ): it bakes only own contour shapes that only move, whose data no other shape shares and that include no other shapes, and composes every other shape. The write never calls layer.applyTransform : the one-argument Python binding also moves the guides, scales the advance and moves every anchor. Anchors move in place, only when the user asks. An existing anchor that would land on 0, 0 blocks Apply: anchor_writer.on_origin is the shared Redo rule (FontLab issue 8527), here with a tolerance of ORIGIN_NEAR because FontLab may round the stored point. The read-back accepts the same tolerance for rounded nodes and anchors. Why: Transform and Slant used private copies of this code. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( affine , anchor_writer , outline_writer ) at load time. PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.contours.transform.ui , so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.transform.model as outline_transform class Slant(outline_transform.panel_type()): def preview_matrix(self, layer): return matrix, guide_y def planner(self): return lambda glyph, master, layer: outline_transform.transform_changes( layer, matrix, True, "250" ) def editor(self): return outline_transform.TransformEditor()

text: bakes ( shape : Any ) -> bool True when FontLab's own layer transform writes the new nodes into the shape. FontLab's rule ( fllayer.cpp:6957-6978 ): an own contour shape whose transform only moves, whose outline data no other shape shares and that includes no other shapes gets new node positions. Every other shape (components, shared data, scaled shapes) keeps its nodes and gets the composed shape transform. This function follows that rule and also composes a shape with no contours, which FontLab would bake. That is harmless: such a shape has no nodes to write.

text: transform_changes ( layer : Any , matrix : Affine , anchors : bool , note : str ) -> list [ Change ] Rows for one layer: the shapes, then the anchors when asked. Shape edit: ("shapes", [(shape, new shape transform, bakes, probe)]); probe is (first node, its expected glyph position) for a baked shape. Anchor edit: ("anchors", [(anchor, x, y)]). An anchor that would move onto 0, 0 blocks Apply: FontLab cannot redo that move (fl#8527). The rule is anchor_writer.on_origin : the new point counts with the ORIGIN_NEAR rounding tolerance, the old point only when it is exactly 0, 0. So an anchor at (0.3, 0) that moves to (0, 0) is refused; only an anchor that is exactly on the origin already does not count.

text: Public queue disclosure and refusal guards for scripts that write to the current font. What: queue disclosure for ordinary writers, and four checks that raise ValueError before any native write. require_selection_window(package_id) : the active panel is a Font window of the bound font (FontLab issue 8528: selection writers crash while a Glyph window is active). require_no_editors() : no Glyph editor is open, also an inactive one (the Unicode save-cache gap of the duplicate-Unicode writer). require_settled() : FontLab has no queued native glyph updates (FontLab issue 8537: queued cache updates become semantic edits later). require_history_scope(glyphs, creates=...) : no Glyph window is the active canvas, or every owner glyph is in that canvas and no glyph is new (FontLab issue 8573: from a Glyph window, the Undo step covers only the glyphs that the canvas shows). fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit , fontlabapp.glyphs.creation.create_glyphs and the eight App writers that call notifyChangesApplied directly call it. How: the selection and editor guards delegate to the reviewed private implementation ( scripting._require_selection_window , duplicate_unicodes_capture.require_no_editors ); require_settled reads the native queue once; require_history_scope reads the text blocks of the active canvas once. The implementations load only when a guard runs, so this module imports only the standard library and FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Why: scripts must not import private App names. Use these guards through fly.ap.core.edit_guards . fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit discloses the queue by default; settled=True explicitly opts into refusing it. Never normalise unrelated dates. Offline tests do not prove native behaviour.
title: fontlabapp.core.edit_guards
